description.p: OpenSSL Encrypt is a comprehensive encryption tool that provides military-grade security with cutting-edge post-quantum cryptography. Protect your files against both current and future quantum computing threats.

ul.li: Multiple symmetric encryption algorithms (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Fernet, etc.)
Post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM, HQC, Kyber) for quantum-resistant protection
Advanced password protection with multiple KDF options (Argon2, PBKDF2, Scrypt)
Secure file operations with military-grade secure deletion
Comprehensive cryptographic hash support (SHA-3, BLAKE2b, Whirlpool)

description.p: Perfect for individuals and organizations requiring the highest levels of data protection, including protection against future quantum computer attacks.
To report bugs or request features, send email to: issue+world-openssl-encrypt-2-issue-+gitlab@rm-rf.ch

Major release. BREAKING: removes deprecated algorithms entirely (AES-OCB3, Camellia, Whirlpool, PBKDF2 chain, legacy Kyber naming) — decrypt such files with v1.4.x first. Large code-surface reduction (steganography, D-Bus, in-package test framework and advisory config tooling removed). New: real 192-bit XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonces, PIV / PKCS#11 HSM backend, source-code integrity protection (verify-integrity with a PGP-signed manifest), ASCII armor output (encrypt --armor, paste-safe PEM Base64 with CRC-24, auto-detected on decrypt), encrypt-to-self (the sender is added as a recipient by default so they can decrypt their own outbound files; opt out with --no-encrypt-to-self), detached post-quantum file signing (sign / verify-signature with ML-DSA-65, adding authenticity that symmetric AEAD alone cannot provide), and read-only interop decryption of age and OpenPGP files (decrypt --from age|pgp) to ease migration, covering both passphrase-based (gpg -c) and public-key (RSA + ECDH) OpenPGP messages. SECURITY FIX: cascade + streaming encryption no longer reuses one cascade salt across chunks (which reused per-layer AEAD nonces); each chunk now derives a unique salt, while legacy files remain readable and are flagged for re-encryption. New opt-in envelope encryption (--envelope) that encrypts data under a random key wrapped by the password, enabling fast credential rekey (rewrap the key instead of re-encrypting the file) and a foundation for multi-password access; for a cascade chain the wrap uses the same chain so it is never the weak link. Full backward-compatible decryption of files made with supported algorithms.
